explanation: Mathlib's `lequivProdOfRightSplitExact` (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Biproducts.lean, l.179) is defined via the universe-lifted private `lequivProdOfRightSplitExact'`, `ShortComplex.Splitting.ofExactOfSection` and `biprodIsoProd`, and comes with no `_apply`/`@[simp]` lemma; grepping the whole Mathlib tree for `lequivProdOfRightSplitExact`, `SplitExact`, `ofExactOfSection`, and `isoBinaryBiproduct_inv`/`Splitting` apply-lemmas turns up only the two definitions (!LeftSplitExact/RightSplitExact) and their uses in Algebra/Module/PID.lean, no statement of the forward formula `(x,b) ↦ j x + g b`. The only concrete tool available is `ModuleCat.biprodIsoProd_inv_comp_fst/snd`, so deriving the formula requires unfolding the definition, pushing the ULift equivalences and combining the splitting's biprod description — exactly the multi-step `change`/`rw`/`simp only`/`rfl` argument the library itself performs (its desc-analogue exists only for AddCommGrpCat, not ModuleCat). No Mathlib declaration carries the theorem's content, so no duplicate or one-line specialization was found.
